subject.title: macOS chat window: native redesign with sessions sidebar, toolbar pickers, slash commands, context usage

question: Should the macOS chat window move from the current compact single-column WebChat shell to the proposed native split-view/session-management design, and which subset should land first?
rationale: The current source confirms meaningful gaps, but the requested fix changes product UX and transport/API behavior across a broad macOS chat surface, and the issue is protected by the maintainer label.

options.title: Stage the native redesign
options.body: Approve the direction but land it as smaller owner-reviewed PRs for sidebar/session actions, command catalog support, context visibility, and visual chrome.

options.title: Transport fixes first
options.body: Prioritize sessions.create/listCommands/patch/delete support before redesigning the full window so current UI actions stop degrading into reset-only behavior.

options.title: Defer the redesign
options.body: Keep the existing compact native WebChat and track only narrow parity fixes if maintainers do not want a larger native shell yet.

recommendation.title: Stage the native redesign
recommendation.body: Approve the direction but land it as smaller owner-reviewed PRs for sidebar/session actions, command catalog support, context visibility, and visual chrome.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the live issue and has the strongest recent history on the macOS/shared chat implementation.
